سَخِيمَةٌ (S, K) and ↓ سُخْمَةٌ (K) Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite; (S, K;) and anger in the soul: (S, TA:) pl. of the former سَخَائِمُ. (TA.) [See two exs. in the first paragraph of art. سل.] ―
-b2- And the former, by a metonymy, is used as meaning (tropical:) Excrement, or dung: so in the trad., مَنْ سَكَّ سَخِيمَتَهُ فِى طَرِيقِ المُسْلِمِينَ لَعَنَهُ ٱللّٰهُ (tropical:) [Whoso voids his excrement in the road, or path, of the Muslims, him God curses]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
